title: Santa lands by helicopter in Torrance, Harbor Glow opens, and Hermosa gets a Ferris wheel
intro: Rain Thursday, then a dry weekend (a small chance of showers Sunday evening). Harbor Glow opens Friday in San Pedro. Saturday, Santa flies into Torrance by helicopter at Robinson, Hermosa puts a Ferris wheel on Pier Plaza, and Long Beach has a free kids' fishing derby. Sunday, Hermosa lights its tree at dusk. Thanksgiving week has a kids' turkey trot and a marina tree lighting with fireworks. Parking, food, and prices are blank unless an official page confirmed them.

picks.name: Santa Takes Flight: Torrance Santa Float Kickoff
picks.when: Saturday, November 21, 4:00–8:00 p.m. (Santa lands by helicopter around 4:30 p.m.)
picks.cost_math: Free; register ahead on Eventbrite (Torrance Police Foundation). Photos with Santa, food trucks, and the Christmas market cost extra if you buy anything; prices not listed. Parking not listed, so no total. Bring a new, unwrapped toy for the police and fire toy drive if you can.
picks.food: Food trucks and specialty food vendors serving dinner, desserts, and treats (organizer). Prices not listed.
picks.why: Santa flies in on a Robinson helicopter to start the Torrance Santa Float season, with photos with Santa, TUSD school choirs, a European-style Christmas market, and kids' activities.

picks.price_text: Free; Ferris wheel $8 per person per ride
picks.name: Hermosa for the Holidays
picks.when: Saturday–Sunday, November 21–22. Ferris wheel noon–9 p.m. both days; free Santa photos Sunday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; tree lighting with Santa's arrival Sunday 5:45–6:15 p.m.
picks.cost_math: Free to attend. Ferris wheel: 1 ride = 4 tickets × $2 = $8 per person, card only, sold at the on-site booth (official) → 4 riders = $32 if you ride. Carnival games (Saturday) vary in price. Santa photos Sunday are free; digital photos arrive a week later (official). Downtown parking rates not listed, so no total.
picks.parking: Downtown Hermosa structures and meters; rates not listed on the event page.
picks.food: Downtown restaurants; hot cocoa, cookies, and activities at the Nonprofit Giving Village on Pier Plaza Sunday 1–6 p.m. (official).
picks.why: A Ferris wheel on Pier Plaza with ocean views, a Letters to Santa station, free Santa photos Sunday, and a tree lighting at dusk Sunday. The downtown Elf on the Shelf hunt wraps up Sunday.

picks.price_text: Timed tickets; price varies by night
picks.name: Harbor Glow at West Harbor (opening weekend)
picks.when: Opens Friday, November 20; nightly through January 3. Fri–Sun 5:00–10:30 p.m., Mon–Thu 5:30–9:30 p.m.
picks.address: West Harbor at Port of Los Angeles, 1332 S Harbor Blvd
picks.cost_math: Timed tickets with a 30-minute entry window. Price varies by date: weeknights are cheaper than weekends, and day-of prices are higher (official FAQ). Ages 3–12 child ticket, 13+ adult, under 3 free with a reserved free ticket. The official site doesn't list a flat price, so we didn't estimate. Premium Parking is an optional add-on priced at checkout.
picks.parking: Harbor Glow Premium Parking lot at the entrance, added with tickets (price shown at checkout, spaces limited). Or West Harbor's public lot, first come, first served, paid on site at West Harbor rates (official).
picks.food: No outside food except baby food and medical or dietary needs; no alcohol (official). West Harbor restaurants nearby.
picks.why: A new walk-through light show on the water: a crystal winter world, then a glowing underwater one. Most families spend 40–60 minutes; strollers and wagons are welcome.

picks.name: Autumn Festival at the Aquarium of the Pacific
picks.address: Aquarium of the Pacific, 100 Aquarium Way
picks.cost_math: Included with general admission (official): 2 × $49.95 + 2 × $34.95 = $169.80, plus $8 validated parking = $177.80, about $178. Under 3 free. Reservations required.
picks.parking: Aquarium Parking Structure: $8 for the day with Aquarium validation (official).
picks.food: Aquarium cafe, or The Pike and Shoreline Village nearby.
picks.why: The aquarium's 25th annual celebration of Asian cultures, with music, dance, and storytelling performances through the day.

picks.name: Long Beach Youth Fishing Derby
picks.when: Saturday, November 21, 9:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. (on-site registration from 8 a.m.; raffle at 1 p.m.)
picks.address: El Dorado East Regional Park, 7550 E Spring St (Area 2, Model Boat Lake)
picks.cost_math: Free for kids 18 and under; poles and tackle provided (City of Long Beach). Park vehicle entry is waived for event participants. Teens 16+ need a California fishing license.
picks.parking: Vehicle entry to El Dorado East Regional Park waived for participants (official).
picks.why: A free learn-to-fish morning with gear and volunteer help, so it works even if your kids have never held a rod. There's a free prize raffle at the end.

picks.name: A Season to Sparkle: Tree Lighting & Santa Arrival at 2ND & PCH
picks.when: Tuesday, November 24, 5:00–8:00 p.m. (moved from November 19 for rain). Tree lighting with Santa 6:00–6:30 p.m., then fireworks.
picks.address: 2ND & PCH, 6400 E Pacific Coast Hwy (on Seaport Way)
picks.cost_math: Free; RSVP to be eligible for a kids' light wand (first come, 3–5 p.m. pickup, while supplies last). Parking: first 90 minutes free, then $2 per 20 minutes (organizer).
picks.parking: On-site; first 90 minutes free, then $2 per 20 minutes (organizer).
picks.food: Center restaurants; activities continue until 9 p.m. (organizer).
picks.why: A 51-foot tree by the marina, Santa and Mrs. Claus, crafts, balloon art and character meet-and-greets, then fireworks.

picks.name: Long Beach Turkey Trot and Kids 1/2-Mile Wingding
picks.when: Thursday, November 26 (Thanksgiving). Kids 1/2-mile: 8:40 a.m. (ages 8–12) and 8:50 a.m. (7 and younger). 5K/10K starts 7:30 and 9:10 a.m.
picks.address: Granada Ave. boat launch ramp, 5000 E Ocean Blvd
picks.cost_math: Kids 1/2-mile is $35 per kid through Nov 26, plus a card service charge (organizer): 2 × $35 = $70, using free street parking. Parents running with kids also register for the Wingding; a 5K/10K entry is $50 through Thursday, Nov 19, then $55. Parking is extra (about $2/hour in the beach lots).
picks.parking: Beachfront lots with 1,000+ spaces, kiosks about $2/hour from 8 a.m.; street parking free; 2nd St. meters usually free on Thanksgiving (organizer).
picks.food: Hundreds of holiday pies given to finishers (organizer). Bring a food-drive item if you can.
picks.why: A flat beachfront course with a short kids' race before the feast. Strollers are welcome and costumes are encouraged.

picks.name: Riviera Village Holiday Stroll
picks.address: Riviera Village, S Catalina Ave (Avenue I to S Elena closed to cars)
picks.cost_math: Free to attend. Parking is metered or paid (price not listed), so no total.
picks.parking: Metered triangle lot between Avenida Del Norte and S Elena, street meters, flat-rate paid parking at Plaza Riviera (1611 S Catalina Ave), and a paid lot at Mira Mar Park (201 Paseo de la Playa). Rates not listed (organizer).
picks.food: Shops serve refreshments while open late; Village restaurants (book dinner ahead, the organizer says).
picks.why: The street closes for a carousel, Santa and the Grinch, a maker's market, and lots of lit-up photo spots.

picks.name: LA Harbor Holiday Boat Parade
picks.when: Saturday, December 5, 6:00–8:00 p.m. (about 90 minutes for the boats to pass)
picks.address: Port of Los Angeles Main Channel, Wilmington to San Pedro
picks.cost_math: Free to watch from shore (official). Parking depends on where you watch; not listed.
picks.parking: Not listed. Viewing spots include the Cruise Ship Promenade (Harbor Blvd. & Swinford St.), LA Maritime Museum (600 Sampson Way), West Harbor (1100 Nagoya Way), and Banning's Landing in Wilmington (official).
picks.food: Not listed; West Harbor and waterfront restaurants are near several viewing spots.
picks.why: Decorated boats light up the harbor, starting near Banning's Landing in Wilmington and heading up the Main Channel toward San Pedro.

picks.name: San Pedro Spirit of the Holidays Parade
picks.address: Downtown San Pedro: 13th St & Pacific Ave, right on 6th St, ending at 6th St & Palos Verdes St
picks.cost_math: Free to watch (San Pedro Chamber). Parking not listed.
picks.why: An afternoon parade with high school bands, scouts, little leagues, and horses, early enough that little kids are home before dinner.

picks.name: Friday Fun at Madrona Marsh
picks.address: Madrona Marsh Nature Center, 3201 Plaza del Amo
picks.cost_math: Free every Friday (Friends of Madrona Marsh).
picks.parking: Nature Center lot. No fee listed.
picks.why: Story time, science, art, and a short tour for preschoolers ages 3–6 with a grown-up.

picks.name: Angels Gate Fall Open Studios Day
picks.address: Angels Gate Cultural Center, 3601 S Gaffey St
picks.cost_math: Free, all ages; RSVP requested (Angels Gate). Art for sale is optional. Parking not listed, so no total.
picks.why: Peek into 50+ artist studios, watch the Teen Mural Club paint, and make a paper bird at the all-ages Wish Upon A Wing workshop.

picks.name: Salt Marsh Open House at Cabrillo Marine Aquarium
picks.address: Cabrillo Marine Aquarium, 3720 Stephen M White Dr
picks.cost_math: Free, all ages; kids must be with an adult (CMA). Cabrillo Beach parking is paid; current rate not listed, so no total.
picks.parking: Cabrillo Beach lot (paid). Rate not confirmed for this date.
picks.why: Educators hand out binoculars and magnifiers to look at the birds and critters in Cabrillo's own wetland.

picks.name: Cabrillo Tidepool Walk
picks.address: Cabrillo Marine Aquarium, 3720 Stephen M White Dr (walk to the Point Fermin tidepools)
picks.cost_math: Free, all ages; kids must be with an adult (CMA). Cabrillo Beach parking is paid; current rate not listed, so no total.
picks.parking: Cabrillo Beach lot (paid). Rate not confirmed for this date.
picks.why: A short orientation, then a naturalist-led walk to the Point Fermin tidepools. Wear sneakers.

picks.name: Visit Long Beach Christmas Tree Lighting (free tickets drop Mondays)
picks.when: Monday, December 7, 5:00–8:00 p.m. Ticket drops Mondays at 10 a.m.: November 23 and November 30 are the last two.
picks.address: Terrace Theater Plaza, 300 E Ocean Blvd
picks.cost_math: Free, but tickets are required (Visit Long Beach), limit four per person. Parking not listed.
picks.food: Food trucks and seasonal treats (official). Prices not listed.
picks.why: A 67-foot tree, falling snow, Nutcracker dancers, free holiday train rides, Santa photos, and fireworks. Set an alarm for the Monday 10 a.m. ticket drop.

picks.name: Redondo Beach Tree & Menorah Lighting
picks.when: Tuesday, December 8. Tree lighting 4:30 p.m., menorah lighting 5:35 p.m.
picks.address: Redondo Beach City Hall, 415 Diamond St
picks.cost_math: Free; complimentary hot chocolate, sweets, latkes, and jelly donuts (City of Redondo Beach). Parking not listed.
picks.food: Complimentary hot chocolate, sweets, latkes, and jelly donuts (official).
picks.why: Two lightings in one evening, with Redondo school choirs and bands.

picks.name: Skechers Manhattan Beach Holiday Fireworks
picks.when: Sunday, December 13, 3:00–8:00 p.m.; fireworks at 7:00 p.m. (rain or shine, barring severe weather)
picks.cost_math: Free. Snow Park entry (4–6 p.m. for the public) is a donated unwrapped toy or canned food item (official). Parking not listed.
picks.parking: Not listed on the event site; downtown streets close for the event.
picks.food: Downtown restaurants; bring a picnic for the beach.
picks.why: Snow Park for kids, a Santa float on Manhattan Avenue, carolers, and a 7 p.m. fireworks show over the pier.
